content.title: Dialogue Comedy | Alternating Singles, Pause, and Reply
content.summary: Use stable alternating singles for one speaking turn from each subject, separate the turns with a clear pause, then return to the first subject for an extended silent expression or gesture.

quick_start.input_format: Stable two-person spatial relationship + complete first dialogue turn + clear pause + short second response + extended silent reaction
quick_start.recommended_input: Two night-shift museum guards hold a locked table axis in matching singles. A states that the alarm is malfunctioning. After a clear pause, cut to B for one brief reply; then return to A, who silently looks at an empty display case and freezes.
required_anchors: Maintain one locked-off table axis with matching eye lines.
Ensure the first dialogue turn is visibly complete before a clear pause.
Insert a silent expectation slot following the second dialogue turn.
Conclude with the first subject's non-verbal response, without an additional dialogue turn.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Two-person dialogue scenes that use a stable shot/reverse-shot axis, one complete speaking turn from each subject, a readable pause, and a final silent reaction from the first subject.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Use stable alternating singles for two visible speaking turns, separate them with one clearly readable pause, then return to the first subject for a final silent facial or posture response. The source evidence supports turn order, pause and reaction only; any sincerity, advice, literalness or joke premise belongs to the new instance and must not be presented as source-derived meaning.

invariants.rule: Keep one stable table axis and matching eye lines.
invariants.purpose: Makes the alternating singles feel continuous.

invariants.rule: Make the first speaking turn visibly complete before one readable pause.
Keep the second speaking turn compact and minimally gestured.
invariants.ablation_failure: A long second performance flattens the final return.

invariants.rule: Insert a silent expectation slot after the second turn.
invariants.purpose: Allows the reply to land visually.
invariants.ablation_failure: An immediate reaction cut feels mechanical.

invariants.rule: End on the first subject's non-speaking response without an additional speaking turn.
invariants.ablation_failure: A third line restarts the exchange.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: source exact facial beats and camera boundaries
